entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: I've been getting a lot of students[n]coming in ever since I arrived here.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: To be honest, it's been... kind of a relief.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: That whole mess with Kamoshida was the[n]reason I was called here, after all...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: They warned me a lot of students had[n]been impacted. I knew there would be[n]a lot of free-floating anxiety.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: But when I actually got to talk to[n]everyone, I was pleasantly surprised.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Most of the things on everyone's minds[n]were college entrance exams,[n]relationship problems...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: In other words, typical worries for high-[n]school students. Some did open up about[n]deeper issues, but not the majority.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Some students were still struggling with[n]the scars from the incident, yes...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: But at the very least, I'm glad the ones[n]who came to me have taken some steps[n]towards recovery.
So they have, huh?[clr 27]
You worry too much.
Thanks to you, probably.[clr 27]

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Well, that's not to say I've gotten a sense[n]of every single student's emotional state.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Either way, I hope my worries end up[n]being groundless after all.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Maybe. It'd be nice if my worries[n]were groundless after all.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Well, I can only hope so!

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: I don't think I've done much, but if I've[n]helped even one person, then that[n]makes it all worth it.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: I know I'm not the most reliable guy, but[n]remember you can always talk to me too[n]if something's bothering you.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: I am the counselor here, you know. If[n]nothing else, I'm good at listening.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Having said that, it's a little awkward that[n]I have to ask for your help, but...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: You remember how I asked you[n]to help me with my research?
Of course.[clr 27]
Yeah, for our deal.[clr 27]
I forgot.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Ahaha! Always quick with a joke,[n][lName]-kun!

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: ...That, uh... was a joke, right?

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: I said you'd be helping with my research,[n]but don't worry. It won't be anything too[n]difficult or intensive.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: I just need you to listen to what I have to[n]say, and work through some questions[n]with me.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: I said you'd be helping with my research,[n]but don't worry. It won't be anything too[n]difficult or intensive.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: I just need you to listen to what I have to[n]say, and work through some questions[n]with me.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: But let's see... Maybe I should start at the[n]beginning. I can tell you a little about[n]what this research is for.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: What I'm studying now is pain felt in[n]the mind. Or perhaps more fancifully,[n]in the heart.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Some specific examples include the pain[n]of someone saying hurtful things to you,[n]or being separated from those you love...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Maybe this would be clearer—pain[n]defined by abstracts, like trauma or[n]stress.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Bodily, physical pain can be thought of[n]as something necessary. An autonomic[n]response to injury, illness, whatever.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: But what about pains felt within[n]one's heart?

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: That pain isn't born from any tangible[n]problem in our bodies, right? It's[n]something strange and immaterial.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: I guess it goes to show there are still a[n]lot of mysteries in our own hearts and[n]minds.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: And I... well, I want to learn more about[n]these internal, psychological pains.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Now, this is my question to you... When[n]do you truly feel pain in your heart,[n][lName]-kun?
When someone betrays me.
When I lie.
When I get punched.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: I see... Yes, I can sympathize there.[n]Sometimes, all it takes is one betrayal for[n]intense trust to turn into intense pain.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: ...That's true. That twinge of guilt is a good[n]example of internal pain.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: So that's not just bodily harm for you?[n]You feel an emotional impact as well?[n]Fascinating.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: It can be rough. It doesn't feel good[n]to struggle with pain in your heart.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: But with that in mind... How about the[n]pain of a broken heart, then?

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: After all, that kind of pain is only born[n]because we fall in love, right?

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Do you have any thoughts on this kind[n]of pain, [lName]-kun?
That one seems necessary.[clr 27]
We'd be better off without it.
It's a seed for new loves.[clr 27]

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: True. It proves and validates the love that[n]came before it, after all... A very fitting[n]answer from you.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: I see... You know, my perspective is[n]actually pretty similar.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Hahaha... I never took you for a poet.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: But it's a wonderful sentiment. A very[n]positive way of looking at it.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Internal, emotional pain can be difficult[n]to deal with. Though some say it's[n]always coupled with other feelings...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: And I agree, of course. I think that's a[n]fair assessment.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Though personally speaking... I'd think[n]if pain can be avoided, it should be.[n]Maybe it shouldn't exist at all.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Wounds of the heart are much harder to[n]detect, and in a way, they're far more[n]complex than physical injuries.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: That's why I'm doing this research... To[n]save people who are suffering from[n]internal pain they keep holding onto.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: You helped me realize that purpose[n]again. Thank you.
Did that help?[clr 27]
Don't worry about it.[clr 27]

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Of course! Thanks to you, I can articulate[n]my thoughts for once.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Thanks to you, I think I'll be able to[n]better articulate my thoughts today.
I can sense Maruki's gratitude[n]towards me...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: ...Okay, I think that'll do for today.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Hm...? Why do I feel like I'm forgetting[n]something...?

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Oh...! Your mental training!

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Oh, uh, no! I didn't forget about our[n]promise, of course!

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: I'll teach you tricks for mental discipline,[n]and you help me with my research![n]Just like we decided, right?

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Now then... how about something like[n]this today?

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: O-Okay, NOW we're ready to wrap things[n]up...
